extracted.intended_audience: general readers of Schiller; translators, editors, and publishers of translated classical works
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative statements about assembling, translating, and presenting Schiller's works in English — covering qualities of historical writing, criteria for good translations, editorial practices for collected editions, and Project Gutenberg redistribution/license requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucidity of style
rubrics_metrics.description: “admirable lucidity of style” — a key quality recommended for historical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preface praises Schiller's 'admirable lucidity of style' as a reason his historical writings are recommended as popular expositions; clarity of expression is presented as essential for communicating history to general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and impartiality of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: “soundness and impartiality of judgment displayed in his historical writings”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sound, fair-minded judgment is highlighted as a determinant of the value of historical exposition; impartiality increases the work's trustworthiness and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability as a popular exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The works are recommended 'as popular expositions of the periods of which they treat.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical writing should be both accurate and accessible — presented so lay/readership can understand and be instructed without specialist prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and accessibility of a collected edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The edition is described as 'the best collected edition ... accessible to readers in the English language.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collected edition should be as complete and as corrected as possible for its target readership; accessibility (language and presentation) is an explicit editorial goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation fidelity vs. readability (literalness tradeoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting that one translation 'was too strictly literal for general readers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translators/editors must balance literal fidelity with readability; overly literal renderings may be unsuitable for general readers and should be revised or rewritten to communicate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful revision and selective rewriting of translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some translations 'have been carefully revised, and some portions have been entirely rewritten.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may revise earlier translations to improve clarity or suitability for new audiences; wholesale rewriting of problematic passages is acceptable when improving readability or accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for prior translators (minimal, sparing revisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier translations 'have been revised, but, in deference to the translator, with a sparing hand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising published translations, preserve the original translator's voice and choices where possible; make limited changes out of respect for the earlier translator while correcting clear issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication and marking of textual variants and restorations
rubrics_metrics.description: Coleridge's version 'contains many passages not found in the printed edition. These are distinguished by brackets.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should explicitly mark passages that differ from other source texts (e.g., bracketed insertions, notes) so readers can see what is original, restored, or variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of source text provenance when translating
rubrics_metrics.description: Coleridge translated 'from a prompter's copy in manuscript, before the drama had been printed, and Schiller himself subsequently altered it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translators should note whether they are working from manuscript/prompter's copies, early drafts, or printed editions; provenance can explain differences and omissions and should inform editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of difficulty/untranslatability and translator skill
rubrics_metrics.description: The Camp of Wallenstein is called 'the most untranslatable of Schiller's works' yet the version cited is an 'exceedingly happy version.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some works present particular translation challenges; successful translations are assessed by the translator's ability to render difficult material naturally and appropriately in the target language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of contextual essays/theory to frame works
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefacing The Bride of Messina with 'Schiller's Essay on the Use of the Chorus in Tragedy' to present the author's theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the author's essays or critical apparatus helps readers understand theoretical or aesthetic context; editorial framing improves comprehension of the primary texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of notable variant passages (restore omissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coleridge's and Mellish's versions included passages not in printed editions; the edition 'has been prefixed' restored or added passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should consider restoring notable passages omitted in later printings if source material (e.g., prompter's copy) supports their authenticity or importance, and indicate such restorations clearly.

rubrics_metrics.description: Do not unlink or detach or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from this work, or any files containing a part of this work or any other work associated with Project Gutenberg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any redistribution that retains the Project Gutenberg association must include the full license text with the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: prominent license sentence on access/display
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed: the specified sentence about use and the Project Gutenberg License 'must appear prominently' with active links or immediate access to the full License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors must display the exact required opening sentence prominently and provide immediate access to the full license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: format conversion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you provide the work in a format other than 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' or the official format, you must at no additional cost provide a copy or means to obtain the original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' form and include the full Project Gutenberg License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate formats are allowed but must include the full license and must not impede access to the original authorized format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: charging fees and royalty conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access unless complying with paragraph 1.E.8 (royalty 20% of gross profits, refund obligations, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial redistribution is possible only under strict conditions including payment of a 20% royalty of gross profits, refund and defect-replacement procedures, and compliance with the full license terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg: defect/disclaimer and limited replacement remedy

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors should be aware that Project Gutenberg provides works 'AS-IS' with a limited replacement/refund policy for defects reported within 90 days; include and follow the stated procedures if offering paid access.
